title: Name the resolution failure when a Bash write-guard target cannot be resolved

truths: A Bash write-guard refusal for a target with unexpanded shell syntax ($VAR, backquote) names the resolution failure and quotes the raw token
No unresolvable token ever appears inside the gate 'writing X is blocked' sentence as if it were a path
The guard stays fail-closed: every previously refused command is still refused

action: Per docs/history/guard-refusal-wording/CONTEXT.md D1-D3: (D1) before canonical_rel_path in the Bash branch (main.rs:189-207), classify a target token carrying unexpanded shell syntax (a $ or backquote) as unresolvable so it never resolves as a literal relative path and never reaches the gate 'writing X is blocked' sentences; (D2) the unresolvable-target refusal states the target could not be resolved and quotes the raw token — sharpen GENERIC_BASH_CONTAINMENT_MESSAGE or add a distinct message in hook_local.rs; (D3) regression tests: a Bash command with an unexpanded $VAR/... target refuses with the resolution-failure wording (not a fake path), and existing resolved-path refusal wording is unchanged. Guard stays fail-closed: the change may only widen the unresolvable bucket, never allow a write.
acceptance: Unresolvable Bash target refusal names the resolution failure and quotes the raw token; no fake path in gate sentence; regression tests green; suite green

trace.outcome: Bash write-guard classifies unexpanded shell-syntax targets (, backquote) as unresolvable and refuses them with a distinct resolution-failure message quoting the raw token, instead of a fake resolved path
